clusters.title: Onboarding assumes a config repo that already holds its own config-project spec, and no step, command or journey says how the first one is made.
clusters.scenario: A newcomer creates an empty repo and runs romeu init --config-url; romeu sync <cfg> then fails because projects/<cfg>.yaml is missing, and every spec edit in 09 is an [A] step in a sandbox that cannot exist yet.
clusters.change: Add J1 step 0: [O] create the config repo from the starter in examples/ (CC0, 00 0.4): copy it into a new repo, edit projects/<cfg>.yaml by hand, push. In 02 2.1 name examples/ as the adopter's starter. In 04 4.2, romeu init row: 'needs an existing config repo whose ref holds projects/<cfg>.yaml (J1 step 0)'. No --scaffold flag.
clusters.cost: A J1 step, a 02 2.1 phrase, a 04 4.2 cell; the J1 scenario treats step 0 as a precondition it checks.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply in the smaller form: the J1 step 0 by hand from examples/ and the 02 2.1 and 04 4.2 sentences; no new init flag.

clusters.title: The clean-exit promise of 00 0.1 and 08 8.1 has no journey, guide or test: nothing says how to stop using romeu and julieta and what is left behind.
clusters.scenario: One user deletes $HOME/dev and loses memory and unpushed salvage payloads; another removes the binaries and leaves sandboxes, egress rules, volumes, refs/romeu/* in every clone and the ledger behind, unaware they exist.
clusters.change: Add 'J14 Stop using romeu and julieta': 1. [O] push or recover unpushed work (J10 step 3); 2. [O] romeu retire each project (J7); 3. what stays on purpose: host clones as plain clones, memory as plain Markdown (03 3.9), $ROMEU_ROOT/.attic; 4. [O] what the operator removes by hand and how: host settings, host state, the ledger, romeu-applied egress rules, refs under refs/romeu/ and refs/sandboxes/ (git for-each-ref plus git update-ref -d), and any remaining sbx sandboxes and volumes. Its scenario runs after J7 and checks git fsck on each host clone, no ref left under refs/romeu/ or refs/sandboxes/ after step 4, and that every memory file parses as 03 3.9 without julieta. S7 covers it as one more journey; its guide page follows the rule of the 09 opening.
clusters.cost: One journey, one scenario function, one guide page; no new success criterion.
clusters.operator_reason: Declines the S12 that R8-index-22 proposes; a success criterion is scope, so the three clusters go to the operator as one decision, SC16, routed by the gate review of the round page.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply J14 as proposed, but without a new S12: the journey is covered by S7 like every other journey, which keeps the criteria count unchanged.

clusters.title: 09 disagrees with itself on J12 (opening: J1 steps 3-6; J12: J1 steps 1-5), names cmux, a non-goal host multiplexer, in J3, and J10 step 3 points at a 'hardened form' no page defines.
clusters.scenario: The guide author follows the J12 section, the scenario author follows the opening, and the rule 13 check passes both because it reads neither range; the J10 guide copies a command whose hardened form exists nowhere.
clusters.change: Opening: replace 'J12 runs J1 steps 3-6' by 'J12 runs J1 steps 3-5 and J12 step 2 (J1 steps 1-2 are installs, preconditions it checks)'. J12 step 1 stays 'J1 steps 1-5 on the new machine'. J3: drop '(for example a cmux window)', leaving 'one terminal window'. J10 step 3: replace '(docs show the hardened form)' by a pointer to an existing path: 'romeu pull and the review checkout of J4 show the salvaged heads; the operator creates and pushes the branch with the hardened git flags of 05 5.1'; if 05 5.1 lists no operator-typable flags, J10 step 3 keeps only the romeu pull and review-checkout half.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed: one J12 range in both places, drop cmux, and J10 step 3 points at an existing path instead of an undefined form.

clusters.title: No journey covers sbx (or its runtime) updated on the host, the most frequent upstream change: gate 1 exits 3 everywhere and no guide says what to check or when the recordings stop describing this sbx.
clusters.scenario: sbx updates overnight; every romeu sync and run exits 3; the operator approves the toolchain without knowing whether the version is inside the tested window or how to roll back.
clusters.change: Add a fourth bullet to J9: 'sbx update on the host: the next romeu sync or run exits 3 (gate 1, 04 4.2); [O] romeu doctor shows the new sbx version against the floor and the recording set (10 10.3); romeu approve --toolchain. A version the recording set does not cover is untested: doctor says so, and the operator either accepts it or reinstalls the previous sbx; a later command that fails on a changed sbx output is recovered with J6 (salvage, --accept-loss) or J10.' J1 step 1: replace '>= v0.46.0' by 'at or above the floor of 10 10.3 (initial v0.46.0)'.
clusters.cost: A J9 bullet and a J1 phrase; the J9 scenario gains a toolchain-change case on the host suite.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as a J9 bullet rather than a new journey, which keeps one journey for every upstream bump.

clusters.title: The spec does not say what a journey passing means in CI or which steps a fake-sbx run omits, so S7's 'every journey passes' has no per-journey meaning.
clusters.scenario: The J3b CI scenario reaches 'then attach', which the fake sbx cannot perform, asserts nothing about the argv or the generation record, and is reported as passing.
clusters.change: Add to the 09 opening: 'In CI a scenario asserts, at each [X] step, the argv romeu passes to the fake sbx, and at each [H] step the state and ledger records the step writes; a step the fake cannot perform (attach, a live daemon fetch) is asserted by its argv only and listed in the scenario's omitted steps, which the host suite covers.' S7 cites this sentence.
clusters.cost: Two sentences in 09, a cite in S7; no per-journey table.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as one rule in the 09 opening instead of a per-journey table; each scenario lists its own omitted steps in code.

clusters.title: One person is 'operator', 'maintainer', 'developer' and 'user' across pages, none is in the vocabulary, and the only sentence relating them is in ADR 0008 Context.
clusters.scenario: A second adopter reads 'the maintainer's approval' in 05 5.3 and 'the operator decided' in 05 5.4 and concludes the product has two roles, one of which they must find.
clusters.change: Add to 01 1.7 the rows operator (runs romeu on a host, owns host settings, answers the gates), maintainer (merges and releases the product repository), developer or user (the operator as 00 0.2 counts them), and 'today one person holds both roles'. 09 legend: link [O] to the operator row. Use each word only in its sense across the pages. ADR 0008 is not changed.
clusters.cost: Three rows and a word pass.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed; ADR 0008 is only cited, not changed. Owned by the page 01 consolidation; on 09 only the legend link.

clusters.title: J1 has no step and no recovery for the dedicated signing agent that git-ssh-sign requires, so sync exits 2 with RJ-204 and the guide has nothing for it.
clusters.scenario: The operator adds git-ssh-sign to a project and sync exits 2 with RJ-204 signing-socket; the J1 guide has no step for it.
clusters.change: Add to J1 step 5: '[O] for a project that uses git-ssh-sign, start the dedicated signing agent with exactly one key and set signing.agentSocket (06 6.4); sync exits 2 with RJ-204 signing-socket until it is reachable and holds that key.' The scenario treats the agent as a precondition it checks.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as a sentence in J1 step 5 pointing at 06 6.4, not a new journey; keeping the agent alive across reboots stays in the guide page.

clusters.title: J1 shows nothing of the trust model before the host is changed, and the README trust paragraph it would rely on has no stated content.
clusters.scenario: An evaluator wants to know, before installing, what romeu will execute and write on their Mac; the README gives a paragraph the spec does not define.
clusters.change: In 12 12.8, README outline cell: the trust paragraph states what romeu writes (host settings, the root tree, host state), what it never does (links to boundaries A-F and I1-I3), and links the product half of 05 5.4. J1 step 1 opens with '[O] read the README trust paragraph'.
clusters.cost: An outline cell and a J1 phrase.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply, with the paragraph linking 05 5.4 instead of restating three chosen risks, so there stays one list.

clusters.title: The maintainer's release flow (rehearsal, rc tag, block B on both hosts, signing, v1.0.0, B1 again, acceptance) is not a journey, so it has no scenario, guide or per-error recovery.
clusters.scenario: At the rc the maintainer pieces the order together from 10 10.2, 11 11.2 and 12 12.2, runs B1 on v1.0.0 with --out inside the repository and overwrites the candidate's result.
clusters.change: Add to the 09 opening: 'Journeys are the operator's; the maintainer's release flow is the ordered checklist of 12 12.2, which names each step's command and output path.' The --out hazard is fixed where 12 12.2 or 11 11.2 names the B1 output path.
clusters.cost: One sentence, plus a path in 12 12.2 if missing.
clusters.resolution_text: State as a limit: the release flow stays a 12 12.2 checklist, not a journey; one sentence in 09 says so.

clusters.title: 09 names two readers against ADR 0001 rule 1, and its steps are written for the scenario writer while the guides copy them for the operator.
clusters.scenario: The J6 guide inherits the [H]/[X]/[J] notation and internal steps (generation open -> salvaging) and omits what the operator sees on the terminal.
clusters.change: Line 3: 'Reader: implementers of the scenario functions. Each guide page in docs/guide/ rewrites its journey for the operator: the commands typed and what the terminal shows, without the step tags or internal states.'
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed on 09; the other pages with two readers are handled when T006 moves readers to front matter.

clusters.title: On the sync --from <sha> path the gate 2 diff is the only review of an unmerged spec, and J2 does not say so.
clusters.scenario: The operator approves a gate for a branch spec expecting a later PR review to catch fields the gate does not show, and the branch is never merged.
clusters.change: Add to J2 step 2: 'On the --from path the gate 2 diff is the only review before the spec applies; fields outside the widening set (for example run) apply unreviewed inside the sandbox.'
